name: Introduction and overview — CH-47 Chinook — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — CH-47 Chinook
description: Introduction and overview of the CH-47 Chinook: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The CH-47 Chinook is a twin-engine tandem-rotor heavy-lift helicopter built by Boeing Vertol, entering service in 1962 and still in production. Its two counter-rotating rotors eliminate the need for a tail rotor. It lifts artillery, vehicles, and up to 55 troops, and remains the U.S. Army's heavy-lift helicopter. Baseline facts: Tandem-rotor heavy-lift helicopter; service from 1962; still in production by Boeing..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
